A Physician Assistant/Nurse Practitioner functions as part of the interdisciplinary healthcare team in accordance with privileges approved by the credentialing committee to provide high quality, cost effective care to patients within the APPs scope of practice in collaboration with a supervising physician. The APP reflects the mission, vision, and values of the organization, and complies with all relevant policies, procedures, guidelines and other regulatory and accreditation standards.

Responsibilities:
1. Clinical- Obtains relevant health and medical history, performs thorough physical assessment, reviews and interprets pertinent diagnostic tests/results. Develops appropriate differential diagnoses. Develops and implements treatment plans including prescribing/ordering of appropriate evidence-based pharmacological agents consistent with departmental guidelines and privileging, and schedules appropriate follow-up management. Actively incorporates evidence-based hospital initiatives to improve patient care. Conducts preventive health screening based on age, history and patient needs. Maintains clear comprehensive yet concise records of all aspects of patient care. Maintains essential knowledge of general disease and pathologic processes. Maintains extensive knowledge of their specialty literature including awareness of developing areas. Consistently derives correct diagnoses through synthesis of clinical data and proper selection and interpretation of diagnostic studies. Develops comprehensive differential diagnoses for patients. Revises the plan of care to meet the changing needs of the patient. Prioritizes work and assists staff to provide prompt and efficient client flow. Consistently maintains high productivity according to identified standards. Leads/participates in projects to improve productivity. Appropriately performs medical procedures consistent with departmental guidelines, privileging, and clinical roles/responsibilities.
2. Education- Appropriately and professionally educates clients and/or families regarding medical condition, treatment, and follow-up. Collaborates with clinicians, staff, and students to promote continuity and patient/family centered care. Develops educational materials based on learning needs of clinicians, staff, and students. Provide education/instruction to physicians, housestaff, nursing, ancillaries and/or students. Actively recognizes and participates in identification and achievement of self-learning needs. Attends education programs based on identified learning needs.

Leads/participates in systems improvements.

Interacts collaboratively with coworkers, other team members and staff in a respectful, courteous, and timely fashion appropriate to patient care needs and situations. Job Location

Duke University Hospital

Job Summary

Hematology is searching for an APP to assist with the hospitalized hematology consult patient service. The APP will round daily on the hematology consult service team which will improve communication with consulting services and patients. The utilization of an APP as part of the consult team within the Division of Hematology would increase the accessibility of care in the hospitalized setting. The current schedule of physicians and fellows in Hematology make daily visits with all consult patients extremely challenging. Incorporating an APP as part of the consult team who understands the nuances of hematology would increase patient and consulting team satisfaction. The APP would be responsible for seeing several new patients each day as well as having a group of follow-up patients seen each day. Efficiency and coordination of patient discharges would improve which in turn would also improve patient satisfaction and safety. Timely and appropriate management of treatment related side effects would also be facilitated by this individual.

Job Duties & Responsibilities

• Daily rounding with the Hematology Consult Service to include presentation of new and follow-up patients as indicated; round with the Hematology attending on patients who need to be seen by the attending; coordinate efforts with the Hematology fellow on service to divide up new Hematology consults who will be followed by the APP; coordinate efforts to provide coverage (with the Attending) for the Hematology fellow when they are in their outpatient clinic.
• Take patient histories, conduct physical examinations, and record the data in the patient’s record; write progress notes; prepare patient workups and summaries noting pertinent positive and negative findings; obtain psychosocial history relevant to patient care, and assume responsibility for developing therapeutic relationships with patients.
• Order and schedule relevant laboratory studies and diagnostic procedures for the workup of hematologic disorders seen in the inpatient setting; explain necessity, preparation, nature and anticipated effects of scheduled diagnostic and therapeutic procedures to the patient.
• Perform bone marrow aspirates and biopsies on patients who need this procedure as part of their diagnostic evaluation.
• Coordinate efforts with the Hematology outpatient triage service to facilitate discharge from the hospital with timely outpatient follow-up with the appropriate provider.
• Share pager coverage with the fellow to provide coverage for medication approvals, follow-up on laboratory results, etc

Education

• Physician Assistants: Completion of an accredited Physician Assistant program. A Bachelor's degree required; Master's degree strongly preferred.

• Physician Assistants: Must be licensed in the state of NC, and be certified as a Physician Assistant by the National Commission on Certification of Physician Assistants.

Experience

• 1+ years of APP experience strongly preferred. Having some background in hematology would also be preferred but not necessary.

Job Hours

• Monday-Friday, 8 am to 5 pm with possibility of administrative time off every week (1/2 day per week to catch up on coordination of outpatient follow ups for example)
• Open to 4 day inpatient week coverage
• Open to 4 day inpatient rounding with 1 outpatient day allowing for a discharge clinic facilitating inpatient-to-outpatient transition

Job Location

Duke University Hospital

Job Summary

We are seeking an Advanced Practice Provider (Nurse Practitioner or Physician Assistant) for the Adult Electrophysiology (EP) unit at Duke University Hospital. The APP will work in collaboration with attending physicians and the EP care team to provide direct care to cardiology patients, with a primary focus on EP patients in the Cardiovascular Short Stay pre-procedural and post-procedural areas. The APP performs physical examinations, obtains procedural consent, collects and documents clinical data, conducts approved diagnostic and therapeutic procedures, orders and schedules laboratory studies and professional consultations, prescribes appropriate interventions and medications, and contributes to excellence in patient care, research, teaching, and leadership.

Primary hours are four 10-hour shifts per week for a 40-hour work week. Hours and days may vary based on service needs and may be adjusted by Heart Center Leadership in consultation with clinical service line leadership.

Job Duties & Responsibilities

• Evaluate new, consult, and established cardiovascular patients ages 16 years and older during the pre-procedural, post-procedural, and/or perioperative phases of care; diagnose, treat, and manage common conditions in the cardiovascular patient population.
• Obtain and document patient histories and physical examinations; prepare patient workups, progress notes, and summaries; document pertinent positive and negative findings; obtain relevant psychosocial history; and develop therapeutic relationships with patients and families.
• Order and schedule laboratory studies and diagnostic procedures; explain the necessity, preparation, nature, and anticipated effects of scheduled diagnostic and therapeutic procedures.
• Obtain informed consent for appropriate procedures and conscious sedation for assigned patients, and discharge procedural patients as directed by the attending physician, including discharge summaries, patient education, and discharge orders.
• Assess patients for changes in clinical status and initiate appropriate interventions, including emergency stabilization and preparation for transfer to the Emergency Department, Operating Room, or inpatient setting when needed.
• Collaborate closely with the EP Lab Charge Nurse, Outpatient Discharge (EOD) Service, inpatient rounding teams, lab fellows, physicians, and other members of the interdisciplinary team to allocate workload and meet daily clinical and operational needs.
• Perform or assist with approved procedures after competency validation, which may include venous and arterial blood sampling, peripheral IV insertion, venous/PICC line removal, urinary catheterization, wound management, urgent/emergent defibrillation or cardioversion, tilt testing, implantable loop recorder insertion, sheath removal, temporary permanent pacemaker dressing changes, and pacemaker/ICD interrogation.
• Administer and manage ordered infusion therapy and medications within scope of practice, including IV fluids, anticoagulants, analgesics, antibiotics, antiarrhythmics, antihypertensives, inotropes, electrolytes, blood products, and nutrition therapies.
• Participate in education, training, evidence-based practice, quality improvement, and research activities; support the education of patients, families, staff, learners, and trainees.

Education

Nurse Practitioners: Work requires completion of an accredited graduate-level Acute Care Nurse Practitioner program.

Physician Assistants: Work requires graduation from a Physician Assistant program accredited by the Accreditation Review Commission on Education for the Physician Assistant (ARC-PA) or its predecessor agencies.

Certification

National certification as an Acute Care NP or certification by the National Commission on Certification of Physician Assistants (NCCPA), as applicable.

BLS and ACLS certification required.

License

Nurse Practitioners: Current licensure as a Registered Nurse in the state of North Carolina and approval to practice as an Acute Care Nurse Practitioner.

Physician Assistants: Current licensure as a Physician Assistant in the state of North Carolina.

Experience

At least one year of experience as an Acute Care NP or PA in cardiology/electrophysiology is strongly preferred.

Job Hours

Full-time salaried position, 40 hours per week; four 10-hour shifts. Hours and days may vary based on service needs.

Overview

The Gastroenterology outpatient/inpatient care Physician Assistant or Advanced Practice Nurse (APN) assists, monitors, and manages the day-to-day needs of patients as requested by, in conjunction with, and under the supervision of a physician. Performs the duties and responsibilities of a Physician Assistant/Nurse Practitioner according to customary and generally accepted medical standards.

Position is located in Manahawkin, NJ.

Office hours:

M-F 8:30-5:00

No weekends required.

No holidays required.

No on-call requirement.

Very busy GI practice with three GI physicians and three APPs.

Responsibilities

1. Provide medical services under the supervision of a licensed physician, consistent with the PA's education, training and experience. 2. Performs and documents accurate, complete, and relevant history and physical assessments appropriate for the patient's age, gender, and clinical problem. 3. Orders, performs, and interprets laboratory tests and diagnostic studies/procedures in collaboration with physicians and consultants as appropriate. 4. Manages general medical and surgical conditions based on comprehensive knowledge of etiologies, risk factors, pathophysiology, and the indications and contraindications of pharmacologic agents and other treatment modalities. 5. Prescribes medication safely and effectively in accordance with best practices, hospital policy, and NJ regulations, providing patient education as needed. 6. Seeks opportunities to promote Hackensack Meridian Health (HMH) PA practice recognition (locally, nationally, and internationally) through conferences, publications, and presentations. 7. Provides care that is patient- and family-centered, compassionate, and effective for the promotion of health and treatment of disease. 8. Practices as a healthcare provider according to the rules and regulations of the Medical Staff and bylaws as outlined in the delineation of privileges. 9. Applies evidence-based and value-based medicine to systematically analyze and improve patient care practices and outcomes. 10. Evaluates patient/family transition of care planning, considering resource utilization, cost, quality, safety and self-management promotion for chronic conditions. 11. Demonstrates clinical expertise through advanced assessment and procedural skills pertinent to the practice specialty. 12. Translates `best practice' into clinical practice by evaluating current protocols and standards of care. 13. Provides culturally sensitive and educationally appropriate health management education to patients and families. 14. Facilitates consistent, coordinated care and clear communication among all members of the healthcare team through participation in daily interdisciplinary rounds. 15. Serves as an advocate for patients and families, identifying and addressing obstacles to care progression and escalating issues as appropriate. 16. Serves as a clinical resource for the multidisciplinary team by addressing clinical, process, and system improvement opportunities. 17. Participates in organizational and departmental meetings, committees, and workgroups as necessary. 18. Demonstrates the highest level of accountability for professional practice and adheres to ethical principles regarding patient confidentiality, informed consent, and adverse outcomes. 19. Promotes a collaborative work environment supporting the organizational mission, behavior expectations, values, and pillars. 20. Mentors other PAs, precepts students in PA programs and participates in educational programs as a clinical expert. 21. Identifies patient/family educational needs and collaborates to implement appropriate teaching materials. 22. Promotes innovation by integrating new clinical knowledge into practice. 23. Participates in clinical research activities and disseminates findings through practice, education, presentations, and publications. 24. Identifies ethical care issues and coordinates interdisciplinary meetings to resolve them. 25. Comply with HMH and department-specific scope of services, policies and procedures as applicable to role. 26. Adheres to all HMH infection control and safety policies. 27. Other duties and/or projects as assigned. 28. Adheres to HMH Organizational competencies and standards of behavior.

Qualifications

Education, Knowledge, Skills and Abilities Required: 1. Successful completion of an approved physician's assistant program, accredited by the AMA Council on Medical Education. 2. Excellent written and verbal communication skills. 3. Proficient computer skills that include but are not limited to Microsoft Office and/or Google Suite platforms.

Licenses and Certifications Required: 1. Physician Assistant License. 2. National Commission on Certification of Physician Assistants. 3. BLS AHA Basic Health Care Life Support HCP Certification. 4. AHA Advanced Cardiac Life Support Certification.

Education, Knowledge, Skills and Abilities Required: 1. Graduate of an NLN/AACN accredited nursing program. 2. Master's or Doctorate degree from an accredited Nurse Practitioner program. 3. Maintains clinical competencies through continuing education and clinical practice. 4. Experience in a relevant patient care setting (or as regulations dictate). 5. National Provider Identifier (NPI). 6. Prescriptive authority through CDS and DEA registration according to New Jersey state law. 7. Collaborative agreement with physicians on staff. 8. Excellent written and verbal communication skills. 9. Proficient computer skills that include but are not limited to Microsoft Office and/or Google Suite platforms. Licenses and Certifications Required: 1. NJ State Professional Registered Nurse License. 2. Advance Practice Nurse License. 3. BLS AHA Basic Health Care Life Support HCP Certification. 4. Board certified by AANP or ANCC. Licenses and Certifications 5. Advanced Cardiac Life Support Certification.

Minimum rate of $146,348.80 Annually

Come Experience an Exceptional Care Delivery Model at One Health!

One Health is an innovative group of providers delivering patient-centered care throughout the Piedmont region of North Carolina. We invite board-certified/board-eligible Nurse Practitioners and Physician Assistants to discover what is possible when compassionate, evidence-based medicine, value-based care, and team member wellness come together to improve the health of our communities.

About One Health

One Health is an independent, physician-led medical group with its own governance structure and leadership, intentionally designed to amplify clinician voice and support excellent patient care. One Health partners with Advocate Health, one of the nation’s largest nonprofit integrated health systems, to enhance access, strengthen resources, and support high-quality care across the region while maintaining One Health’s independent, provider-led model.

One Health currently operates 35 primary care offices across the greater Charlotte and Winston-Salem areas of North Carolina. Our specialties include Family Medicine, Internal Medicine, Pediatrics, Sports Medicine, Rheumatology, OB/GYN, and Urgent Care.

As a provider-led organization, One Health focuses on provider joy, reducing total cost of care, human experience, financial excellence, and care for all. Providers are supported by a strong operational infrastructure while retaining meaningful clinical autonomy, allowing them to focus on what matters most: delivering exceptional care, building lasting relationships, and making a meaningful impact in the communities they serve.

Position Highlights

We are seeking a dedicated Nurse Practitioner or Physician Assistant to join the Family Medicine team at Atrium Health One Health Mount Island. This position will provide high-quality, comprehensive primary care during extended weekend hours, expanding access and providing greater flexibility for patients and families in the Mount Island community.

Schedule: Friday, Saturday, and Sunday, 7:00 a.m. – 7:00 p.m.

This unique three-day schedule offers the opportunity to provide full-spectrum family medicine while helping One Health expand convenient access to primary care.

Responsibilities

• Provide comprehensive, patient-centered family medicine care across a broad spectrum of ages, disease states, and chronic conditions.
• Evaluate, diagnose, and treat acute illnesses and injuries within the scope of outpatient family medicine.
• Manage chronic conditions and provide preventive care, health screenings, and patient education.
• Develop individualized treatment plans using evidence-based clinical practices.
• Coordinate care with physicians, specialists, clinical team members, and other healthcare professionals as appropriate.
• Support continuity of care through appropriate follow-up, referrals, and care coordination.
• Utilize One Health and Advocate Health resources, technology, and clinical support services to enhance patient care.
• Contribute to a collaborative practice environment that values clinical expertise, teamwork, and an exceptional patient experience.

The Ideal Candidate Will Be:

• Passionate about providing high-quality, patient-centered primary care.
• Comfortable caring for patients with a wide range of acute and chronic healthcare needs.
• Experienced in Family Medicine, Primary Care, or a related outpatient setting.
• Committed to working the Friday, Saturday, and Sunday extended-hours schedule.
• Dedicated to collegiality, professionalism, compassion, personal growth, and leadership development.
• Interested in practicing within a collaborative, provider-led organization that values clinical autonomy and team-based care.

Why North Carolina?

The Piedmont region of North Carolina offers an exceptional quality of life with options ranging from vibrant urban communities to charming small towns. Enjoy excellent schools, affordable living, abundant outdoor recreation, and convenient access to Charlotte, Winston-Salem, the Blue Ridge Mountains, and the Carolina coast.

Why Join One Health?

When you join One Health, you become part of a culture that values the contributions of every team member. Practice in an environment where your work is recognized, your input is valued, and your commitment to advancing patient care is supported with the resources needed to succeed both personally and professionally.

Our Commitment to You

Advocate Health offers a comprehensive suite of Total Rewards, including competitive compensation, robust benefits, career development opportunities, and programs that support your well-being both at work and at home.

• Competitive base compensation based on qualifications, skills, relevant experience, and training.
• Premium pay opportunities, including on-call and other eligible differentials.
• Incentive compensation for select positions.
• Annual compensation increases based on performance.

Benefits and More

• Generous Paid Time Off programs.
• Medical, dental, vision, life, short-term disability, and long-term disability coverage.
• Flexible Spending Accounts for eligible healthcare and dependent care expenses.
• Family-focused benefits, including adoption assistance and paid parental leave.
• Defined contribution retirement plans with employer matching contributions.
• Financial wellness resources and planning tools.
• Educational Assistance Program to support ongoing professional growth.

Join One Health Mount Island and help us expand access to exceptional family medicine care for the patients and communities we serve.

Atrium Health is seeking an experienced, full-time Advanced Practice Provider specializing in Behavioral Health to provide comprehensive psychiatric and behavioral health services to patients requiring acute psychiatric evaluation, consultation, and treatment.

This position is open to board-certified Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioners (PMHNP-BC) and Physician Assistants (PA) who are trained and proficient in the delivery of psychiatric services. Full-Time
Schedule: Variable evenings, nights, weekends, and holidays

Graduation from an accredited Nurse Practitioner program

This position provides essential behavioral health coverage during evening, overnight, weekend, and holiday hours, contributing to improved patient access, continuity of care, and efficient clinical workflows.

When you join Atrium Health, you become part of an inclusive culture that values collaboration, innovation, and compassion. Join our Behavioral Health team and help expand access to timely, compassionate, and comprehensive psychiatric care for the patients and communities we serve.

jobs.summary: Physician Associate/Acute Care Nurse Practitioner - Bariatric and Minimally Invasive Surgery at MaineHealth Barbara Bush Children's Hospital. Notable: relocation assistance.
jobs.description:
The MaineHealth Maine Medical Center Department of Surgery is seeking a collaborative and motivated Advanced Practice Provider (APP) to join our Bariatric and Minimally Invasive Surgery team. This position offers a unique opportunity to work alongside a multidisciplinary team providing comprehensive surgical care to patients throughout their perioperative journey.

The APP will have a broad and dynamic role that includes inpatient management, perioperative care, and operative participation as a first assist in the operating room. Responsibilities include conducting patient assessments, developing and implementing treatment plans, coordinating care across disciplines, managing post-operative patients, facilitating discharges, and providing patient and family education. The APP will work closely with surgeons, residents, nursing staff, and other healthcare professionals to ensure high-quality, patient-centered care.

This full-time position includes rotating weekend coverage and no call responsibilities, promoting a healthy work-life balance. The APP will primarily support the Bariatric and Minimally Invasive Surgery service, with opportunities to provide cross-coverage for the Colorectal Surgery service based on operational needs.

Qualified candidates must be certified as a Physician Associate (PA-C) or Acute Care Nurse Practitioner (ACNP/AGACNP) and eligible for licensure in the state of Maine. Previous surgical experience and first assist experience are preferred but not required.

Join a highly respected surgical team within Maine's largest academic medical center and help deliver exceptional care to a diverse surgical patient population while enjoying the opportunities, resources, and support available through MaineHealth.

• Analytical abilities necessary to obtain medical histories, conduct physical examinations, prepare complex treatment plans, and treat assigned patients with minimal guidance and direction.
• Interpersonal skills and communication skills to engage as a specialist with a variety of personnel (e.g., patients, employees, physicians, and other health care professionals.)
• Knowledge of patient assessment techniques including taking medical histories, performing physicals, evaluating health status, including state of wellness and compliance with care recommendations.

§ Ability to make responsible decisions within scope of practice (ACNP or PA).

The Duke Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology is seeking an Advanced Practice Provider (APP) to join its team of experienced Complex Menopause providers. The APP will deliver evidence-based care, patient education, and counseling that helps patients navigate midlife health concerns. The team includes generalist OB/GYN physicians with Menopause Society certification who will provide mentorship and clinical oversight.

The schedule is variable and may require flexibility, including early-evening and weekend hours to support patient and clinician scheduling needs.

Primary responsibilities

Provide evaluation, management, education, counseling, and treatment for patients with common and complex menopause-related concerns, including:

• Medical management of menopausal health concerns, including menopausal hormone therapy
• Symptomatic perimenopause, including hormonal contraception, IUD use, and cyclic progestogen therapy
• Menopausal and perimenopausal symptom management for patients with hereditary breast and ovarian cancer risk, high-risk cancer patients, and cancer survivors, using hormonal and non-hormonal approaches as appropriate. Patient population may include natural, premature, early, surgical, and radiation-induced menopause
• Menopausal and perimenopausal symptom management in patients with higher-risk conditions, including tobacco use, clotting disorders, cardiovascular disease, valvular disease, liver disorders, and transplant history
• Assessment of abnormal and postmenopausal bleeding
• Menopause-related cognitive and mood changes
• Genitourinary syndrome of menopause
• Midlife vulvar dermatoses and vulvovaginitis
• Midlife weight management
• Sexual health and sexual dysfunction, including desire, arousal, orgasm, genitourinary, and pelvic floor concerns, and related treatment options

Gynecological Care

Based on menopause patient volume, the APP may provide in-person routine gynecologic care and treatment for common concerns including:

• Family planning and reproductive life-planning counseling
• Routine screening examinations and cervical cancer screening
• Referrals for age- and risk-appropriate screening, including mammography, bone density testing, and colorectal cancer screening
• Screening and treatment for sexually transmitted infections
• Evaluation of breast changes or masses
• Evaluation of pelvic or abdominal pain
• Routine postoperative follow-up and problem visits
• Treatment of vulvar cysts and abscesses

Responsibilities may also include in-person assessment and treatment opportunities such as:

• IUD placement and removal
• Endometrial biopsy
• Vulvar biopsy
• Other in-person gynecologic assessments and treatments within the APP’s scope, credentials, and privileges

Job Eligibility Requirements

Education

• Nurse Practitioners: Requires completion of an accredited Nurse Practitioner program, with a Master's degree in Nursing.
• Physician Assistants: Requires completion of an accredited Physician Assistant program. A Bachelor's degree required; Master's degree strongly preferred.
• Certified Nurse Midwife: Requires completion of an accredited graduate-level nurse‑midwifery program at the MSN or DNP level.

Certification

• BLS required

License

• Nurse Practitioners: Must have current or compact RN licensure in the state of North Carolina. National certification as a Nurse Practitioner required.
• Physician Assistants: Must be licensed in the state of NC and be certified as a Physician Assistant by the National Commission on Certification of Physician Assistants.
• Certified Nurse Midwife: Must have current or compact RN licensure in the state of North Carolina. National certification as a Nurse Midwife required.
• DEA license for applicable practice state(s)

The remote care model may support patients across multiple states as program licensure expands. Applicants should identify every state in which they currently hold an active professional license and any compact licensure status, as applicable.

Experience

• Two or more years of experience as a Nurse Practitioner, Physician Assistant or Certified Nurse Midwife in Women’s Health
• Experience managing midlife Women’s Health concerns
• Experience or training in sexual health management and/or prescribing anti-obesity pharmacotherapy
• Certification by The Menopause Society, or comparable menopause-focused training is preferred or must be licensed within six months of employment

Job Location

Duke University Hospital

Job Summary

The Duke Hospital Cardiothoracic Intensive Care Unit (CTICU) Advanced Practice Provider (APP) provides direct patient care services for complex critically ill cardiothoracic surgery and Advanced Heart Failure patients, predominately in an intensive care setting in collaboration with cardiac anesthesiology and under the supervision of the cardiothoracic surgeon(s) and the Medical Director of the CTICU. The APP performs physical exams, collects and documents data, conducts diagnostic and therapeutic procedures, orders and schedules laboratory studies and professional consultations, prescribes appropriate interventions and medications, coordinates the care and discharge of patients, and provides direct patient care services.

Job Duties and Responsibilities

• Provide /coordinate clinical care for cardiothoracic surgery patients at Duke Hospital being followed primarily in the Cardiothoracic Intensive Care setting through established protocols and under the supervision of the cardiothoracic surgeon or back-up supervising physician who is either on site or available by pager
• Patient rounding in collaboration with attending cardiothoracic surgeon(s),cardiac anesthesiologist(s), CTICU intensivists, and Medical Director of the CTICU, round daily on patients to assess, diagnose, plan treatment, set priorities and realistic outcomes, and evaluate the effectiveness and cost efficiency of cardiothoracic patient care;
• Perform procedures when indicated: (Partial listing…full list will be shared upon request or at time of interview)

• Flexible bronchoscopy for non-biopsy purposes in patients with an artificial airway
• Ventilator Management

• Chest tube insertion / management / removal

• Thoracentisis

• Arterial line placement and removal
• Intraortic balloon pump (IABP) removal
• Venous line placement/central line including PA catheter placement, temporary dialysis catheter, temporary transvenous pacemaker
• Venous line removal including temporary dialysis catheters
• Place gastric or post-pyloric feeding tubes
• Management of peripherally placed central and peripheral venous catheters (PICC/C)
• Peripheral intravenous catheter placement (PIV)
• Wound management including wound vac, application of dressings and bandages, simple debridements, suture removal/placement, local cauterization, staple removal/placement

• Management of Mechanical Circulatory Support Device devices
• Collaborate with the chief resident, residents and fellows to formulate treatment plans and monitor patient progress
• Assess patients for change in status and institute appropriate interventions. Initiates emergency interventions in an effort to stabilize the patient until physician support arrives.

Performs and documents accurate, complete, and relevant history and physical assessments appropriate for the patient's age, gender, and clinical problem. 3. Orders, performs, and interprets laboratory tests and diagnostic studies/procedures in collaboration with physicians and consultants as appropriate. 4. Manages general medical and surgical conditions based on comprehensive knowledge of etiologies, risk factors, pathophysiology, and the indications and contraindications of pharmacologic agents and other treatment modalities. 5. Prescribes medication safely and effectively in accordance with best practices, hospital policy, and NJ regulations, providing patient education as needed. 6. Seeks opportunities to promote Hackensack Meridian Health (HMH) PA practice recognition (locally, nationally, and internationally) through conferences, publications, and presentations. 7. Demonstrates the highest level of accountability for professional practice and adheres to ethical principles regarding patient confidentiality, informed consent, and adverse outcomes. 19. What We Offer

Are you ready to join a remarkable team where exceptional care meets exceptional service every patient, every time?

Novant Health Medical Group Heart & Vascular Institute – Cardiac Surgery is seeking an experienced, highly motivated Cardiac Surgery Advanced Practice Provider (APP) to join our Charlotte Region team. This is an outstanding opportunity to work alongside a collaborative and nationally recognized cardiothoracic surgery program dedicated to delivering advanced, patient-centered cardiovascular care.

The ideal candidate will bring prior cardiothoracic surgery experience, including experience with endoscopic and/or open vein harvesting, and a strong commitment to clinical excellence, teamwork, and compassionate patient care. We are seeking a hardworking, dependable APP who thrives in a fast-paced surgical environment and is passionate about improving patient outcomes across the continuum of cardiac surgical care.

In this role, you will work closely with our cardiac surgeons and multidisciplinary care teams to provide high-quality perioperative and postoperative care for cardiac surgery patients. Responsibilities include inpatient management, surgical first assist responsibilities, vein harvesting, and coordination of care throughout the patient journey.

At Novant Health, you will join a mission-driven organization that values innovation, collaboration, and professional growth while offering competitive compensation and a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your personal and professional well-being.

Novant Health Benefits:
• Competitive compensation package
• NH Medical Group employed position
• Comprehensive medical and retirement benefits
• CME allowance
• System-wide Epic EHR
• Malpractice coverage
• Strong focus on work-life balance

Why Novant Health Medical Group?
• One of the largest medical groups in the nation
• Physician-led and physician-driven organization
• APP Council focused on APP engagement, growth, and clinical excellence
• ODYSSEY onboarding and professional development program for physicians and APPs
• Resiliency and wellness initiatives designed to prevent burnout
• Nationally recognized, community-based, non-profit healthcare system known for advanced patient care

What Does It Mean to Be Part of Novant Health?

At Novant Health, patient-centered care is at the heart of everything we do. We are committed to creating a seamless healthcare experience while building meaningful relationships with our patients and communities.

Novant Health is an integrated network of physician clinics, outpatient facilities, and hospitals serving communities throughout North Carolina, South Carolina, and Georgia. Our network includes more than 1,800 physicians and over 35,000 team members across nearly 800 locations, including 15 hospitals.

Novant Health has been recognized nationally for diversity, workplace excellence, and community impact, including recognition by Forbes and the Disability Equality Index.

At Novant Health, diversity and inclusion are core values. By embracing the strengths and talents of every team member, we create a stronger organization capable of delivering remarkable care to our patients, families, and communities.

Join us, and let’s transform healthcare together.

#MakeHealthcareRemarkable #NHMGAPPs

What You'll Do

It is the responsibility of every Novant Health team member to deliver the most remarkable patient experience in every dimension, every time.

• Our team members are part of an environment that fosters teamwork, team member engagement and community involvement.
• The successful team member has a commitment to leveraging diversity and inclusion in support of quality care.
• All Novant Health team members are responsible for fostering a safe patient environment driven by the principles of "First Do No Harm".
• Hours: 8-5p Mon-Fri.
Call responsibilities include one night/week and one weekend/month

• Supporting Locations: Novant Health Presbyterian Medical Center. No travel required.

What We're Looking For

Education: Master's Degree Required. Graduate of an NCCPA accredited Physician Assistant or Nurse Practitioner program required.

Experience: One to three years of experience as a Surgical Advanced Practice Provider required and one to three years of endoscopic vein harvesting experience preferred. RNFA required for NP candidates.

Licensure/Certification/Registration: Current PA license in appropriate state Required. NCCPA Certification and current DEA registry Required. ACLS (if infusion center or cardiac specialty) Required.

Additional Skills Required: Ability to successfully complete generic and department-specific skills validation and competency testing. Ability to work with management team and physicians; demonstrated customer service skills, interpersonal skills and communication skills.

Why Choose Novant Health?

At Novant Health, we believe remarkable care starts with compassion for our patients, our communities, and each other. We value belonging, courage, personal growth, and teamwork, creating a space where everyone is respected, supported, and safe to show up as their full selves.

Overview

The Advanced Practice Nurse (APN) utilizes a patient-centered coordinated care model, demonstrating competencies in leadership, direct clinical practice, consultation/collaboration, coaching/guiding, research, and ethical decision-making. The APN works collaboratively with the practice/hospital team to assess, plan, and implement care for individuals with health and safety needs.

Responsibilities

1. Performs and documents accurate, complete, and relevant history and physical assessments appropriate for the patient's age, gender, and clinical problem. 2. Orders, performs, and interprets laboratory tests and diagnostic studies/procedures in collaboration with physicians and consultants as appropriate. 3. Manages general medical and surgical conditions based on comprehensive knowledge of etiologies, risk factors, pathophysiology, and the indications and contraindications of pharmacologic agents and other treatment modalities. 4. Prescribes medication safely and effectively in accordance with best practices, hospital policy, and NJ regulations, providing patient education as needed. 5. Seeks opportunities to promote Hackensack Meridian Health (HMH) APN practice recognition (locally, nationally, and internationally) through conferences, publications, and presentations. 6. Provides care that is patient- and family-centered, compassionate, and effective for the promotion of health and treatment of disease. 7. Practices as a healthcare provider according to the rules and regulations of the Medical Staff and bylaws as outlined in the delineation of privileges. 8. Adheres to HMH nursing protocols, standards of care, and disease-specific quality indicators. 9. Applies evidence-based and value-based medicine to systematically analyze and improve patient care practices and outcomes. 10. Evaluates patient/family transition of care planning, considering resource utilization, cost, quality, safety and self-management promotion for chronic conditions. 11. Demonstrates clinical expertise through advanced assessment and procedural skills pertinent to the practice specialty. 12. Completes medication reconciliations as appropriate. 13. Participate in annual APN peer review. 14. Translates `best practice' into clinical practice by evaluating current protocols and standards of care. 15. Provides culturally sensitive and educationally appropriate health management education to patients and families. 16. Facilitates consistent, coordinated care and clear communication among all members of the healthcare team through participation in daily interdisciplinary rounds. 17. Serves as an advocate for patients and families, identifying and addressing obstacles to care progression and escalating issues as appropriate. 18. Serves as a clinical resource for the multidisciplinary team by addressing clinical, process, and system improvement opportunities. 19. Participates in organizational and departmental meetings, committees, and workgroups as necessary. 20. Demonstrates the highest level of accountability for professional practice and adheres to ethical principles regarding patient confidentiality, informed consent, and adverse outcomes. 21. Collaborates with medical staff to support nursing-led protocols. 22. Mentors other APNs, precepts students in APN programs and participates in educational programs for nursing as a clinical expert. 23. Identifies patient/family educational needs and collaborates to implement appropriate teaching materials. 24. Facilitates and participates in nursing educational programs as a clinical expert. 25. Promotes a collaborative work environment supporting the organizational mission, behavior expectations, values, and pillars. 26. Promotes innovation by integrating new clinical knowledge into practice. 27. Participates in clinical research activities and disseminates findings through practice, education, presentations, and publications. 28. Identifies ethical care issues and coordinates interdisciplinary meetings to resolve them. 29. Adheres to the legal framework and scope of practice defined by the NJ Division of Consumer Affairs, ensuring compliance with all applicable statutes and professional standards. 30. Comply with HMH and department-specific scope of services, policies and procedures as applicable to role. 31. Other duties and/or projects as assigned. 32. Adheres to HMH Organizational competencies and standards of behavior.

Qualifications

Education, Knowledge, Skills and Abilities Required: 1. Graduate of an NLN/AACN accredited nursing program. 2. Master's or Doctorate degree from an accredited Nurse Practitioner program. 3. Maintains clinical competencies through continuing education and clinical practice. 4. Experience in a relevant patient care setting (or as regulations dictate). 5. National Provider Identifier (NPI). 6. Prescriptive authority through CDS and DEA registration according to New Jersey state law. 7. Collaborative agreement with physicians on staff. 8. Excellent written and verbal communication skills. 9. Proficient computer skills that include but are not limited to Microsoft Office and/or Google Suite platforms. Education, Knowledge, Skills and Abilities Preferred: 1. Not Applicable. Licenses and Certifications Required: 1. NJ State Professional Registered Nurse License. 2. Advance Practice Nurse License. 3. BLS AHA Basic Health Care Life Support HCP Certification. 4. Board certified by AANP or ANCC. Licenses and Certifications Preferred: 1. Advanced Cardiac Life Support Certification.

jobs.description:
Overview

Seeking a dynamic and experienced Psychiatric-Mental Health Nurse Practitioner (PMHNP) to lead our Crisis Behavioral Health nursing department. This leadership role is responsible for overseeing daily operations, managing clinical and support staff, and ensuring the delivery of high-quality, comprehensive care to acute, complex patients. The Manager will serve as a clinical expert, provide leadership to the specialty area, and ensure compliance with all regulatory standards.

• Previous leadership experience is required.
• Certification: PMHNP certification is required.
• Schedule: Full-Time, Monday-Friday, 8:00 AM - 5:00 PM. No weekends.

Responsibilities

• Workflow: Provides administrative support and direction in the day to day operation of the assigned unit. Develops short and long term goals for the unit which are aligned with organizational goals. Manages time and resources effectively by managing multiple priorities with appropriate delegation. Develops, implements, and supports activities and/or projects that promote patient satisfaction within a patient centered care framework to achieve best practice targets. Provides timely notification of critical events to all appropriate individuals according to regulatory and organizational policies and practices. Ensures all team members are knowledgeable in emergency preparedness/disaster response policies and procedures. Develops unit specific response plan and participates in all preparedness drills as required mobilizing unit/department resources to meet needs as required.
• Budgetary Goals: Promotes cost effective use of organizational resources, consistently supporting budget objectives. Responsible for financial analysis at the unit/department level with consideration for case mix, acuity workload, volume, variable staffing plans, personnel and fixed/variable unit costs. Reviews and acts on variance analysis reports including nursing hours per patient day, cost per unit of service, FTEs and other variables. Implements, monitors and evaluates action plans aimed to correct variances for each pay period. Prepares and submits monthly variance and justification reports to Director/CNO on a monthly basis.
• Clinical Mentor: Maintains clinical expertise/credentials while seeking to build on strengths and grow in areas for improvement. Ensures appropriate educational activities are planned and implemented for patients, families, and team members to ensure implementation of evidence based practice, improves educational performance, and meets established standards of care. Provides and supports professional growth opportunities for team members to develop and enhance leadership skills. Recognizes and celebrates team member leadership accomplishments at the individual and unit level.
• Human Resources Management: Maintains and adheres to established policies, procedures and protocols relative to position controls, team member action forms, approved vacancy listings, and other tools/forms used. Gathers information on issues, counsel, employees and initiates timely disciplinary action with appropriate and timely documentation.
• Performance Improvement Goals: Establishes and maintains high standards for quality and service, sharing knowledge expertise with team members as a means to achieve desired results. Develops and implements unit based/house wide projects which enhance patient and family centered care. Collaborates with team members and other departments in implementing strategies to ensure success of PDCA/Performance Improvement projects.
• Effective Leadership: Fosters open, direct, and constructive communication across all levels and departments to eliminate obstacles and meet goals. Demonstrates leadership in fair, unbiased decision making with dependability and reasonable expectations. Maintains composure, values and principles under stressful and dynamic conditions and when faced with opposition or obstacles and acts in an honest, trustworthy and ethical manner.
• Quality Improvement: Manages multiple priorities, meeting deadlines and expectations in quality and regulatory project management. Monitors and evaluates the implementation of standards of nursing care ensuring compliance with regulations from the DOH, JCAHO, Board of Nursing and Magnet Credentialing. Ensures and is accountable for the provision of competent care to patients and families and assures nursing care is delivered and documented through the nursing process. Participates in and implements recommendations provided through Best Care Inspections for regulatory readiness.
• Obtains a thorough patient history that includes: Determination of the chief complaint, analysis of primary symptomatology. Review of the course since onset of above: incidence, progress and effect of therapy(s). Completes medical and social history. Performs an appropriate physical examination and recognizes normal and abnormal findings. Records findings of the physical exam in a clear and concise manner. Makes recommendations based on the data gathered in the history and physical examination for ordering ancillary studies, developing a problem list, formulating a differential or actual diagnosis, counseling, educating and instructing patients in specific disease-related and preventative medicine areas. Orders, interprets, and evaluates diagnostic and laboratory tests to identify and assess patient's clinical problems and health care needs for continuity of care.
• Writes orders to implement non pharmacological and pharmacological therapeutic plans. Communicates with collaborating physicians regarding pertinent patient information including but not limited to actual or potential clinical problems, diagnostic tests/labs, consultants' recommendations, and updates or adjustments to the treatment plan via the multidisciplinary rehabilitation team. Collaborates with physicians, nurses, and other health care team members.
